Description: THE STRONGEST UNRESOLVED LEAD IN THE ERITREA FILE, AND DELIBERATELY NOT CONVERTED INTO A ROW. This is the WHO Eritrea country office year-end bulletin for 2007. Its Figure 6, titled 'Epid Curve of Outbreak of Acute Diarrhoea in Bada, Northern Red Sea, Eritrea', prints a week-by-week table for epidemiological weeks 38-43 of 2007: Cases 3, 97, 46, 33, 10, 1 (total 190); Deaths 0, 2, 1, 2, 0, 0 (total 5). The narrative reads: 'There were also major outbreaks of acute diarrhoeal disease in Asseb and Tio in Southern Red Sea Zoba and as presented in Figure 6, there was another outbreak in Bada, Gelalo sub Zoba of Northern Red Sea.' WHY THIS MATTERS: WHO GHO records Eritrea 2007 = 119 cholera cases and 9 deaths, and WER 83(31) 2008 states 'For the first time ever, Eritrea reported an outbreak that caused 119 cases including 9 deaths' and explains the 7.6% CFR as reflecting 'the difficulty in accessing vulnerable groups living in remote areas in a timely manner'. Bada/Gelalo is a remote Danakil sub-zoba whose population is nomadic pastoralist (WHO Eritrea migratory-route mapping, 30 May 2007, names Bada explicitly), it is the ONLY documented Eritrean non-bloody diarrhoeal outbreak of 2007, and it falls inside the window mid-July to 10 November 2007 for which metadata 96 shows WHO published NO Eritrea bulletin. Bada is also the exact locality of the 12/11/06 Navy rumour 'Cholera across the border - BADA' logged in metadata 68. The Bada outbreak is therefore the leading candidate for the geography of Eritrea's only cholera notification in history. WHY NO ROW WAS WRITTEN, STATED PLAINLY SO NOBODY REVERSES IT CASUALLY: (1) the document says 'Acute Diarrhoea', never 'cholera' and never 'acute watery diarrhoea', and the same document's own guidance box explicitly distinguishes cholera (acute watery) from shigella (bloody), so 'acute diarrhoea' is the generic parent term, not a cholera synonym here; (2) CLAUDE.md's pre-extraction checklist requires the source to mention cholera cases or deaths explicitly, and this one does not; (3) this country file already contains a documented trap of exactly this shape (UNICEF HAC 2017 acute watery diarrhoea read as cholera); (4) the counts do not match - 190 cases and 5 deaths against the national 119 and 9 - so even if the events are identical the numbers are not interchangeable. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the WHO Eritrea bulletins for weeks 29-45 of 2007 (Issue 2 Nos 14-19), which metadata 96 shows were never published or never archived, or the Eritrean MoH IDSR annual report for 2007. FOR AGENT 7 / HUMAN REVIEW: this is the single highest-value adjudication left in ERI - it would geolocate the only cholera Eritrea has ever reported to WHO.
